thread.title: Market Volatility Bulletin: Stacked December Calendar Means Equity Volatility Has Upside Bias

author: The Balance of Trade
title: Market Volatility Bulletin: Stacked December Calendar Means Equity Volatility Has Upside Bias
text:
Market Intro
CNBC: 1:30 PM EST
Energy prices ( USO ) are mostly notching a positive day, which over the last two months or so has definitely served as the exception and not the rule. Friday's market action witnessed a near-8% spill in WTI prices.
A positive tone for the Brexit divorce negotiations may have served as an impetus for rising European equities ( EFA , VGK , EWU ).
US stocks ( SPY , DIA , QQQ , IWM ) are positive for all the major averages, and spot volatility is down modestly in Monday afternoon trade.
SectorSPDR.com
Between Fed speak and economic releases, the next three days do carry potential for reasonably large magnitude equity moves - either higher or lower.
Thoughts on Volatility
I think "they" would, Matt! In fact, that's what the tape has shown as the day has carried on. SPX hit the same level this morning as it hit last week before reversing sharply lower. Thus far, bulls do seem to be in charge of the action, and I would consider it an important victory if they can string together some action atop 2666, which translates to S&P price gains for 2018.
December has some fireworks scheduled. If risk assets have a mind to rattle and hum on news, then policy makers have to really decide how active, and how market friendly a stance they wish to take. In the case of Brexit, I doubt that parliament is going to craft voting decisions based on perceived market responses.
In 2015, we saw the dollar ( UUP ) strengthen and commodities ( DBC , GSG) suffer. As the year wore on, these actions transmitted in a rather important way into junk bonds ( JNK ). High yield spreads tightened quite a bit after the US election, which is to say that Treasury yields moved meaningfully higher and junk yields didn't keep pace.
If recent history is a guide, vol shorts ( SVXY ) will gain some real support if junk yield spreads maintain composure.
Term Structure
That is one flat term structure! The max - min reading is .4 vol points across. Furthermore, the roll yield is essentially zero, and only the HV10 shows real signs of dropping, though HV20 is also showing the lowest reading that it has posted in about a month.
My suspicion is that the early part of December could play out more favorably than the back part. So long as some of the larger names ( AAPL ) can cool down, market seasonality could come to the fore, and give markets the jolt they need.
One item that hints for higher vol ahead is the fact that VIX9D is not taking the opportunity to drop lower, which may indicate higher overall volatility levels ahead. Positive days without a tremendous amount of change in market direction are supposed to take vol down a notch, which has not happened thus far today.
We saw similar stubbornness in the VIX9D the week before the traditionally quiet Thanksgiving period.
Short vol as a swing trade has historically relied on roll yield favoring shorts.
That simply does not exist in the current market environment, and so the case for shorting volatility has to be a call on falling absolute levels in the VX term structure.
I would continue to recommend "renting" vs. "owning" short volatility here.
Conclusion If this is your first time reading Market Volatility Bulletin, thanks for giving it a try. If you're a regular, we thank you for your ongoing contributions in the comments section.
Thank you for reading.
